title: PRD: Tiered quality profiles for hosted inference endpoints (Fast / Accurate)
creator: Sana Iqbal
description:
Summary: Propose and ship a lightweight tiering mechanism on Redwood hosted endpoints that exposes two named inference profiles — 'fast' and 'accurate' — so customers can opt into lower-latency / lower-cost behavior or higher-quality / higher-cost behavior without changing models or client-side logic. This is primarily a product/contract and rollout effort: minimal API surface, clear acceptance criteria, performance benchmarks, observability additions, and launch runbook.

Problem statement: Many customers trade off latency and quality differently across use cases (chat vs. high-precision summarization vs. embeddings for search). Currently they must pick different models or duplicate endpoints to get predictable cost/latency. That results in complexity for customers and higher per-token costs. A first-class, simple profile parameter will reduce cognitive load, improve cost predictability, and allow us to give prescriptive defaults and telemetry for optimization suggestions.

Goals:
- Add an optional 'profile' parameter on hosted inference endpoints (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank) with values 'fast'|'accurate' and a documented default.
- 'fast' should favor lower latency: shorter decoding budgets, lower sampling complexity, and automatic micro-batching heuristics.
- 'accurate' should favor output quality: fuller decoding budgets, diversity/sampling settings tuned for quality, and fallback to higher-capacity model variants where available.
- No breaking changes to existing clients (default behavior remains unchanged unless profile explicitly set).
- Provide clear cost multipliers and benchmark numbers in product docs and Console.

Non-goals:
- Not introducing new model artifacts or requiring new model uploads for GA — profile should map to runtime heuristics and compatible model variants we already host.
- Not a replacement for customer-managed model selection; advanced users can still choose specific models per endpoint.

High-level approach:
- API: optional query param / JSON field 'profile' on relevant endpoints. Server-side will map profile -> runtime config.
- Runtime mapping: engineering will implement a small mapping layer translating profiles to: kernel selection preference, max_decode_length/default temperature, micro-batching windows, KV-cache prefetch policy, and candidate re-ranking toggles for rerank endpoints.
- Console & Docs: document cost/latency/quality tradeoffs, show per-request profile label in Request logs and per-route dashboards, and add a small cost-estimator in the Console.

Customer-facing contract:
- Profile default: if omitted, behave as today (no change).
- Profile is advisory; we guarantee semantic compatibility (same model outputs still possible) but not bit-for-bit determinism.
- Pricing disclosure: 'fast' may reduce per-token effective cost by ~10–30% depending on workload; 'accurate' may increase costs by ~5–25%. We will surface an estimated multiplier in the Console and API response headers on GA.

Metrics & success criteria:
- Adoption: >= 15% of newly onboarded customers opt-in to profiles in first 90 days for at least one route.
- Latency: 'fast' median P95 latency improvement of at least 20% vs default on benchmark chat load profile.
- Quality regression: when using 'accurate' vs default, no statistically significant decrease in standard QA eval suites; 'fast' should have controlled degradation (documented).
- Cost: measurable reduction in per-token cost for customers using 'fast' with typical short-turn workloads.
- Observability: Console shows profile-aware metrics and all production routes tagged within release window.
acceptance_criteria: API: Hosted chat/completions/embeddings/rerank endpoints accept optional 'profile' field with values 'fast'|'accurate' (string) and validate inputs with a helpful 400 message for invalid values.
Backward compatibility: Omitting 'profile' yields identical request handling to pre-release behavior (no config drift), verified by regression suite and sampled production canary traffic.
Runtime: Mappings implemented that produce measurable latency or quality shifts according to profile per the benchmark plan (see links).
Console: Per-route Request logs include 'profile' annotation and a small cost multiplier tooltip; docs updated and linked from Console.
Docs: SDK and API reference updated with examples and recommended uses for each profile.
Benchmarks: End-to-end performance and quality benchmarks for sample workloads published in the PRD and stored artifact; artifacts referenced in the release notes.
Monitoring: New SLO dashboards show profile-aware latency, error rates, token cost, and quality regression alerts tied to eval sets.
Launch checklist: All pre-launch tasks in tasks[] completed and verified by PM and Eng leads.
tasks: Finalize API contract and OpenAPI spec change (PM + Eng) — include profile param docstring and header guidance.
Engineering: Implement profile mapping layer (ENG) + unit tests + runtime flags for canary.
E2E: Create benchmark harness for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank to measure P50/P95 latency and baseline QA metrics for both profiles.
Console: Add profile label to request logs and per-route charting; expose estimated cost multiplier in tooltip.
Docs & SDKs: Update REST docs, Python/TS SDK examples, migration notes, and quickstart examples for using 'fast' and 'accurate'.
Pricing & billing: Coordinate with finance to add profile multiplier to internal cost reporting and sample billing estimator (UI).
Security & compliance: Run a light risk review (dataflow unchanged) and confirm no additional PII concerns for profiling logic.
QA: Regression test plan + integration test with canary traffic; run fuzz tests for invalid profile values.
Rollout: Canary on 5% traffic for 48 hours, monitor quality and latency; expand to 25% then 100% if metrics healthy.
Launch comms: Blog post, release notes, and in-product tooltip with recommended mappings and examples.

notes: Rollout safety: We will implement a server-side kill-switch keyed by release flag to revert profile semantics quickly.
Benchmarks should include both single-request latency and tail behavior during concurrent small-turn workloads to capture micro-batching effects.
We will not surface profile in API telemetry until GA to avoid skewing early experiments. During canary we will tag internal requests for analysis.
